course_name_original: Myślenie krytyczne. Współczesne wyzwania kultury i cywilizacji
course_name_en: Critical thinking. Contemporary challenges of culture and civilization

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the basic paradigms of analysis in social sciences and humanities.
Knows the relationships between processes, structures and social institutions and their elements in contemporary society.
Can interpret texts from the field of social sciences and humanities and, based on this, expand their knowledge of culture and society.
Is aware of the importance of sociological analysis and humanistic reflection for understanding contemporary social, political, economic and cultural processes.

syllabus_topics: What is critical thinking?: The aim of the course is to teach critical thinking: independent, objective, free from ideologies and stereotypes, capable of looking at the studied problem from multiple sides and directions, and the ability to apply this thinking to the analysis of contemporary problems of civilization, culture, social life, and politics. The introductory part will deal with forms of thinking (scientific, mythological, metaphysical-religious thinking) and the determinants of our thinking. In the second, main part, based on selected texts, we will analyze and discuss some contemporary problems, such as: mass society and mass culture, mythology and politics, freedom, responsibility, education, the dispute over historical memory.

Lecture topics list: 1. Map of thinking. 2. Critical thinking 3. Mass society 4. Mass culture 5. Revolution in the value system 6. Social weakness and responsibility 7. Politics and mythology 8. Politics and truth 9. Contemporary university 10. Culture vs. civilization 11. Culture, religion, faith 12. Lies 13. Models of capitalism 14. Models of capitalism
assessment_rules: Learning outcomes are verified by activity during classes. The credit condition for lectures is activity during classes.
